Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0123", "row_sha256": "a24c68757992f71ad8fb1e292c7b9edadda2c86fdd5b945fb161256ae3378fb2", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a clear prompt for a small change to our shared family meal calendar, not a whole new calendar. the week is monday october 13 through sunday october 19, 2025. five of us use it: Nora, Ellis, June, Mateo, and Ruth. Nora and Ellis keep the calendar up to date, but the others can see it and reply in the family chat. please keep the request focused on that one week and the one dinner we are discussing. the calendar is just for coordinating meals, so this isn't about invitations, shopping, or sending anything to a restaurant.

right now the Tuesday October 14 entry says “Family dinner, 5:45 pm, Nora and Ellis's home: baked potato bar.” what i want is to move that existing dinner to Thursday October 16 at 6:15 pm, but only if all five people have individually confirmed in the family chat that Thursday at 6:15 works. the deadline for those replies is Monday October 13 at noon. i mean an actual clear yes from each person, not a guess from their usual routine or someone saying they think another person can come. if even one person's reply is missing or unclear at noon, the condition hasn't been met. the event should stay the same dinner, with the same hosts and meal, and the request isn't to add a second dinner or change the menu while moving it.

there's a reason we're checking rather than assuming. June has a class that sometimes runs late on Thursdays, and Mateo's work shift changes from week to week. Ruth usually has a free Thursday, but that doesn't count as a confirmation for her. Nora and Ellis also need to confirm; being the people who maintain the calendar doesn't mean they have already agreed. The replies can arrive at different times, and they don't have to use identical wording, but each needs to clearly say the proposed date and time work for that person. If a reply says “maybe,” asks a question without answering, or only confirms a different time, treat that person as not confirmed by the deadline. Don't use information from outside this week or make assumptions based on older calendar entries.

for context, the Wednesday October 15 entry is dinner at Ruth's apartment at 6:00 pm, and it is already confirmed. Friday October 17 has no family dinner because Mateo is scheduled to work late. Saturday October 18 is open; we have not picked a meal or host for it. Those entries aren't requests to edit. In particular, don't move the Wednesday meal to cover for Tuesday and don't fill the open Saturday space as part of the main change. The only calendar entry that could be edited under the condition is the existing Tuesday dinner. If the group agrees to Thursday, its date and time change, but it should remain a single event at Nora and Ellis's home.

keep the existing food details in view too. June is vegetarian, and Ruth avoids walnuts. The baked potato bar already works for both of them, so don't replace it with a different meal or add walnuts. June once wrote, “I can bring the soup, but I can't get there before six.” That was about a different evening, so it isn't a confirmation of this Thursday plan and it isn't a request to change the baked potato bar. The proposed time is 6:15, not six on the dot. No one has offered a new side dish for this dinner, and there is no need to invent one in the calendar wording.

1. First check the five replies against the deadline and the exact proposed Thursday time. If every person has clearly confirmed by Monday at noon, make the one requested update to the Tuesday entry: move it to Thursday October 16 at 6:15 pm, retaining Nora and Ellis's home, the baked potato bar, and the fact that it is the same family dinner. Don't change any other event.
2. If any one of the five has not clearly confirmed by then, do not edit the shared calendar at all. Instead, draft a proposed one-week meal plan for the family to review, using the schedule and meal information in this request. Keep it clearly a proposal, not a published or agreed plan; don't claim that anyone approved it.

that second action is only the fallback when the condition fails, not an additional task to do alongside a calendar edit. Keep the proposal useful and limited to this week, preserve the already confirmed Wednesday dinner, and don't invent confirmations, availability, meals, or hosts for the open Saturday. If the information supplied isn't enough to fill a proposed slot, leave it open rather than pretending a decision has been made. In either case, make the result easy to read in the family chat and return only the relevant result: either the updated calendar entry if the condition is met, or the proposed one-week plan if it isn't. No explanation of the checking process or separate commentary.

one other date is already settled and should simply be left alone: Sunday October 19 has brunch at 10:30 am at the park. It is not part of the Tuesday-to-Thursday change, and the final result should not turn it into a new request or suggest that it needs a confirmation check.", "output": "Create a clear, concise result for the shared family meal calendar for Monday, October 13 through Sunday, October 19, 2025. The calendar is used by Nora, Ellis, June, Mateo, and Ruth to coordinate family meals. Keep this request limited to the existing Tuesday dinner; do not create invitations, contact a restaurant, or add shopping information.

Check whether all five people have individually and clearly confirmed in the family chat that Thursday, October 16, at 6:15 pm works. Each person’s reply must be received by Monday, October 13, at noon. Nora and Ellis must confirm as well as June, Mateo, and Ruth. Do not infer agreement from anyone’s routine or from another person’s reply. A missing or unclear reply, a “maybe,” a question without an answer, or agreement to a different time does not satisfy the condition. Do not rely on information from outside this week or older calendar entries.

If—and only if—all five have clearly confirmed by the deadline, update the existing Tuesday, October 14 entry to Thursday, October 16, at 6:15 pm. Keep it as the same single family dinner at Nora and Ellis’s home, with the baked potato bar. Do not change any other event, add a second dinner, or change the menu.

If even one person has not clearly confirmed by the deadline, do not edit the shared calendar. Instead, draft a proposed one-week meal plan for the family to review. Keep it clearly marked as a proposal, not a published or agreed plan, and do not claim anyone approved it. Preserve the already confirmed Wednesday, October 15 dinner at Ruth’s apartment at 6:00 pm. Friday, October 17 has no family dinner because Mateo works late; Saturday, October 18 is open and has no selected meal or host. Do not invent meals, hosts, availability, or confirmations for the open Saturday. If the supplied information is not enough to fill a proposed slot, leave it open. The fallback is required only if the confirmation condition fails; do not provide it in addition to an update.

Keep the food details accurate: June is vegetarian, Ruth avoids walnuts, and the existing baked potato bar works for both. Do not add walnuts or replace the meal. June’s earlier message, “I can bring the soup, but I can't get there before six,” concerned a different evening. It is not confirmation of the proposed Thursday dinner and does not change the menu; the proposed time is 6:15 pm. No one has offered a new side dish.

Return only the relevant result: either the updated calendar entry if all five confirmations meet the condition, or the proposed one-week plan if they do not. Make it easy to read in the family chat, without explaining the checking process or adding separate commentary.

Leave Sunday, October 19 brunch at 10:30 am at the park unchanged. It is not part of the Tuesday-to-Thursday change and does not need a confirmation check."}]
